play.comment: Stephon Castle's step-back three with 43 seconds left that made it 96–90, after De'Aaron Fox rebounded a missed Wembanyama free throw. An original illustration from the play-by-play and written accounts; not traced from footage, not to scale.

aria: Animated recap of the Spurs' 99 to 96 home win over the Lakers: Stephon Castle's step-back 3-pointer with 43 seconds left that made it 96 to 90, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Castle's 26 points and 9 assists, the top scorers, how the Spurs won, and the next game.

figure.label: Stephon Castle, listed 6-6, 215 lb, No. 5 (RealGM); no sourced wingspan

notes: Box score from CBS Sports' gametracker for the Spurs' 99–96 home win over the Lakers on Nov 27, 2026, the last NBA Cup group game for both teams: all 99 San Antonio points and all 96 Los Angeles points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (40 of 86, 10 of 29 from three, 9 of 16 FT for San Antonio; 37 of 86, 12 of 42, 10 of 14 for Los Angeles). Rebounds (56–52, with team rebounds), offensive rebounds (13–11), assists (23–19) and steals (11–10) are CBS Sports' team totals; Bleacher Report's player lines match CBS for every player it lists. The quarter scores (14–24–30–31 to 27–27–14–28) are on CBS Sports; 54–38 Lakers at the half is also in the AP, Bleacher Report and the NY Post. The Lakers' biggest lead, 20 at 45–25 with 4:43 left in the second quarter, is on CBS Sports' play-by-play and in Bleacher Report, the NY Post and the Express-News; the Spurs' 8 (81–73 and 86–78) is on CBS Sports' play-by-play and in the NY Post. Points in the paint and fast-break points are not shown: no page read had them. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Stephon Castle had 26 points on 10 of 15 shooting and 9 assists; Victor Wembanyama had 25 points, 16 rebounds and 4 steals (CBS Sports; Bleacher Report). The Spurs' 14-point first quarter and 38-point first half were their lowest of the season (Express-News); they won the third quarter 30–14 and it was 68–68 after three (CBS Sports; AP). Dylan Harper (hip) and De'Aaron Fox (shin) returned (Express-News). Luka Dončić scored 31 but made 1 of 13 threes (CBS Sports; NY Post). The win sends San Antonio to the NBA Cup knockout round as a wild card and eliminates the Lakers (AP; Yahoo Sports), and it was the Spurs' first win over the Lakers this season (Express-News). Wembanyama: "It just showed character" (Express-News). Next: the Spurs host Boston on Sunday and the Lakers play at Memphis on Sunday (AP; Bleacher Report); the Spurs' Cup quarterfinal is at Dallas on Dec. 4 (Express-News; wire.report).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Stephon Castle's 3-pointer with 43 seconds left that made it 96–90: CBS Sports' play-by-play has "Stephon Castle makes three point stepback jump shot" (no assist) for 93–90 to 96–90, after Wembanyama made one of two free throws at 0:57 and De'Aaron Fox rebounded the miss; the AP has the three at 43.4 seconds after Fox's rebound. The Express-News calls it a corner three, so the spot on the floor is not settled and the step-back is drawn with the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The board's Spurs +3 to +6 is 93–90 to 96–90. Castle: "I had the shot, so I took it" (Express-News). The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the San Antonio Spurs or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Castle's listed 6-foot-6 and 215 pounds (RealGM); no wingspan was found in the sources read, so his arms are drawn at his height. He wears the Spurs' home white with No. 5 (RealGM). He has no look in kit/looks.json yet, so he is drawn with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
